statement: The move planner's over-target ADD cap stops wiping an open priority-spread cure: when the same evaluation computes prioritySpreadGapOpen=true, the planner retains exactly the ADD moves that cure distinct-node spread (targets not already hosting a replica) while still refusing surplus growth, so formation can spread the six priority control-plane partitions instead of stalling at 2/3 distinct nodes. Verified at HEAD c002553ae (live 3-node runs + code trace): in ec-postfix-20260810T060111Z the cap at src/rebalancer/move-planner-move-calculation-methods.js:385-424 fired 40x on control_plane_publications-p1 with activeCount=4 targetReplicaCount=3 activeDistinctNodeCount=2 targetDistinctNodeCount=3 overCreationCap=true prioritySpreadGapOpen=true deferredAdds=1 and unconditionally did addMoves.length=0 at :423 (its own comment names the cure-starvation stall; the diagnostic exists, the guard does not act on it); the replaceSerializationCap wipe at :671-690 fired 58x on replica_operations-p1; net effect 2-3 CREATE_REPLICA per 135s boot, third node receives zero replicas, joiner formation barrier times out. The rebalancer leadership lifecycle and the flat [70,80)s background delay are correct and out of scope; the July drainPhaseReplacementCredit mechanism is wired but does not cover this shape. Fail-closed floor: surplus growth beyond target on an already-spread partition must remain refused, and the drain-phase credit semantics must be preserved.
